# requireValidLocale

<link-summary>Returns the value as a locale code, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireValidLocale() — Returns the value as a locale code, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireValidLocale(
  value: string | null | undefined,
  message: string = "Expected a valid locale."
): string;
```

Exactly two ASCII letters, in either case — `"en"`, `"UK"`. A region or a script subtag, as in `"en-US"`, is rejected: this is the short language code, not a full BCP 47 tag.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                             | Type                          | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                               | `string \| null \| undefined` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a valid locale."` | `string`                      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as a locale code.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                       |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------ |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a locale code. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireValidLocale("en"); // => "en"
requireValidLocale("UK"); // => "UK"
requireValidLocale("en-US"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireValidLocale("eng"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
